++"""Typed tool primitives. Calling a write tool still requires an approval layer.
++
++Web requests connect to a validated DNS result directly, not via a proxy or a
++second DNS lookup. Redirects and compressed responses are intentionally not
++followed/decoded, keeping the public-network and size boundaries explicit.
++"""
++import asyncio
++import ipaddress
++import os
++import re
++import socket
++import ssl
++import uuid
++from dataclasses import dataclass
++from pathlib import Path
++from typing import Literal
++from urllib.parse import quote, urlsplit
++
++import h11
++from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
++
++MAX_FETCH_BYTES = 256 * 1024
++FETCH_TIMEOUT = 10
++
++
++class ToolError(ValueError):
++    pass
++
++
++class WebFetchArgs(BaseModel):
++    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
++    url: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2048)
++
++
++class NotesArgs(BaseModel):
++    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
++    filename: str = Field(min_length=5, max_length=85)
++    content: str = Field(max_length=16000)
++
++
++@dataclass(frozen=True)
++class ToolSpec:
++    name: str
++    risk: Literal['read', 'write', 'send', 'spend']
++    args: type[BaseModel]
++    description: str
++
++
++REGISTRY = {
++    'web_fetch': ToolSpec('web_fetch', 'read', WebFetchArgs, 'Fetch text from an explicitly allowed public website.'),
++    'write_note': ToolSpec('write_note', 'write', NotesArgs, 'Create a text note in this Bot’s workspace.'),
++}
++
++
++def canonical_host(host):
++    try:
++        value = host.rstrip('.').encode('idna').decode('ascii').lower()
++        if not value or len(value) > 253:
++            raise ValueError()
++        return value
++    except (UnicodeError, ValueError) as exc:
++        raise ToolError('Invalid hostname.') from exc
++
++
++def host_matches(host, pattern):
++    suffix = pattern.startswith('.')
++    domain = canonical_host(pattern[1:] if suffix else pattern)
++    return host == domain or (suffix and host.endswith('.' + domain))
++
++
++def validate_target(url, allow, deny):
++    if any(ord(ch) < 33 or ord(ch) == 127 for ch in url):
++        raise ToolError('URL contains invalid characters.')
++    try:
++        parsed = urlsplit(url)
++        if parsed.scheme not in ('http', 'https') or not parsed.hostname or parsed.username is not None or parsed.password is not None:
++            raise ToolError('Use an HTTP(S) URL without credentials.')
++        host, port = canonical_host(parsed.hostname), parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme == 'https' else 80)
++        if not 1 <= port <= 65535:
++            raise ToolError('Invalid port.')
++    except ValueError as exc:
++        raise ToolError('Invalid URL.') from exc
++    if host == 'localhost' or host.endswith('.localhost') or host.endswith('.local'):
++        raise ToolError('Private and non-public addresses are blocked.')
++    try:
++        address = ipaddress.ip_address(host)
++        if not public_address(address): raise ToolError('Private and non-public addresses are blocked.')
++    except ValueError as exc:
++        if isinstance(exc, ToolError): raise
++    if any(host_matches(host, item) for item in deny) or not any(host_matches(host, item) for item in allow):
++        raise ToolError('This website is not allowed by the web fetch policy.')
++    path = quote(parsed.path or '/', safe="/%:@!$&'()*+,;=-._~")
++    if parsed.query: path += '?' + quote(parsed.query, safe="/%:@!$&'()*+,;=?-._~")
++    return parsed.scheme, host, port, path
++
++
++def public_address(address):
++    if isinstance(address, ipaddress.IPv6Address) and address.ipv4_mapped:
++        address = address.ipv4_mapped
++    return address.is_global and not (address.is_multicast or address.is_unspecified or address.is_loopback or address.is_link_local or address.is_private or address.is_reserved)
++
++
++async def _fetch(url, allow, deny):
++    scheme, host, port, path = validate_target(url, allow, deny)
++    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
++    try:
++        resolved = await loop.getaddrinfo(host, port, family=socket.AF_UNSPEC, type=socket.SOCK_STREAM)
++    except OSError as exc:
++        raise ToolError('Could not resolve this website.') from exc
++    addresses = list(dict.fromkeys(item[4][0] for item in resolved))
++    if not addresses:
++        raise ToolError('Could not resolve this website.')
++    try:
++        if any(not public_address(ipaddress.ip_address(address)) for address in addresses):
++            raise ToolError('Private and non-public addresses are blocked.')
++    except ValueError as exc:
++        if isinstance(exc, ToolError): raise
++        raise ToolError('Could not validate website addresses.') from exc
++    # Pass a literal validated address to the socket; never re-resolve a host
++    # after checking it. TLS certificate validation still uses the original host.
++    tls = ssl.create_default_context() if scheme == 'https' else None
++    try:
++        reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection(addresses[0],port,ssl=tls,server_hostname=host if tls else None)
++        try:
++            conn=h11.Connection(h11.CLIENT, max_incomplete_event_size=16*1024)
++            authority=f'[{host}]' if ':' in host else host
++            if port != (443 if scheme=='https' else 80): authority += f':{port}'
++            writer.write(conn.send(h11.Request(method='GET',target=path,headers=[('Host',authority),('User-Agent','FunkBot/1.0'),('Accept','text/plain,text/html,application/json;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.1'),('Accept-Encoding','identity'),('Connection','close')])))
++            writer.write(conn.send(h11.EndOfMessage()))
++            await writer.drain()
++            body=bytearray(); status=None; content_type=''; encoding=''
++            while True:
++                event=conn.next_event()
++                if event is h11.NEED_DATA:
++                    data=await reader.read(8192)
++                    conn.receive_data(data)
++                    continue
++                if isinstance(event,h11.InformationalResponse): continue
++                if isinstance(event,h11.Response):
++                    status=event.status_code
++                    headers={k.decode('ascii').lower():v.decode('latin1') for k,v in event.headers}
++                    content_type=headers.get('content-type','')
++                    encoding=headers.get('content-encoding','').strip().lower()
++                    if status < 200 or status >= 300:
++                        raise ToolError('Website returned a non-success status; redirects are not followed.')
++                    if encoding not in ('','identity'):
++                        raise ToolError('Compressed responses are not supported.')
++                    try:
++                        if int(headers.get('content-length','0')) > MAX_FETCH_BYTES:
++                            raise ToolError('Website response is too large.')
++                    except ValueError as exc:
++                        if isinstance(exc,ToolError): raise
++                        raise ToolError('Invalid response length.') from exc
++                elif isinstance(event,h11.Data):
++                    body.extend(event.data)
++                    if len(body)>MAX_FETCH_BYTES: raise ToolError('Website response is too large.')
++                elif isinstance(event,h11.EndOfMessage):
++                    if status is None: raise ToolError('Website returned an invalid response.')
++                    return {'url':url,'status':status,'content_type':content_type[:200],'text':body.decode('utf-8','replace')}
++                elif isinstance(event,h11.ConnectionClosed):
++                    raise ToolError('Website closed the connection unexpectedly.')
++        finally:
++            writer.close()
++            try: await asyncio.wait_for(writer.wait_closed(), timeout=1)
++            except (OSError, asyncio.TimeoutError): pass
++    except (OSError, h11.RemoteProtocolError, h11.LocalProtocolError, UnicodeError) as exc:
++        raise ToolError('Could not safely fetch this website.') from exc
++
++
++async def web_fetch(args: WebFetchArgs, allow: list[str], deny: list[str]):
++    try:
++        return await asyncio.wait_for(_fetch(args.url,allow,deny), timeout=FETCH_TIMEOUT)
++    except asyncio.TimeoutError as exc:
++        raise ToolError('Website request timed out.') from exc
++
++
++def write_note(data_dir: Path, bot_id: str, args: NotesArgs):
++    """Create only a new file, through non-symlink directory descriptors."""
++    try:
++        if str(uuid.UUID(bot_id)) != bot_id: raise ValueError()
++    except ValueError as exc:
++        raise ToolError('Invalid Bot workspace.') from exc
++    if not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,79}\.txt',args.filename):
++        raise ToolError('Use a simple .txt filename without folders.')
++    if not hasattr(os, 'O_NOFOLLOW') or not hasattr(os, 'O_DIRECTORY') or os.open not in os.supports_dir_fd:
++        raise ToolError('Secure workspace writes are not supported on this platform; use Docker.')
++    flags=os.O_RDONLY|os.O_DIRECTORY|os.O_NOFOLLOW
++    root_fd=workspace_fd=bot_fd=None
++    try:
++        root_fd=os.open(data_dir,flags)
++        try: os.mkdir('workspaces',0o700,dir_fd=root_fd)
++        except FileExistsError: pass
++        workspace_fd=os.open('workspaces',flags,dir_fd=root_fd)
++        try: os.mkdir(bot_id,0o700,dir_fd=workspace_fd)
++        except FileExistsError: pass
++        bot_fd=os.open(bot_id,flags,dir_fd=workspace_fd)
++        fd=os.open(args.filename,os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL|os.O_NOFOLLOW,0o600,dir_fd=bot_fd)
++        with os.fdopen(fd,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='\n') as file:
++            file.write(args.content)
++        return {'filename':args.filename,'bytes':len(args.content.encode('utf-8'))}
++    except FileExistsError as exc:
++        raise ToolError('That note already exists; choose another filename.') from exc
++    except OSError as exc:
++        raise ToolError('Could not safely create the note in this workspace.') from exc
++    finally:
++        for fd in (bot_fd,workspace_fd,root_fd):
++            if fd is not None: os.close(fd)

++// Disposable deterministic OpenAI-compatible gateway for tool E2E tests only.
++import http from 'node:http';
++const port=Number(process.env.MOCK_PORT||8030);
++http.createServer(async(req,res)=>{
++ if(req.method!=='POST'||req.url!=='/v1/chat/completions'){res.writeHead(404).end();return}
++ let raw='';for await(const data of req)raw+=data;const payload=JSON.parse(raw);
++ const lastUser=payload.messages.filter(m=>m.role==='user').at(-1)?.content||'';
++ const hasTool=payload.messages.at(-1)?.role==='tool';
++ const chunks=[];
++ if(!hasTool){
++  const isFetch=lastUser.includes('fetch loopback');
++  const args=isFetch?{url:'http://127.0.0.1:8030/private'}:{filename:lastUser.includes('deny')?'denied.txt':'approved.txt',content:'A real approved fixture note.'};
++  chunks.push({choices:[{delta:{tool_calls:[{index:0,id:'fixture-call',function:{name:isFetch?'web_fetch':'write_note',arguments:JSON.stringify(args)}}]},finish_reason:null}]});
++  chunks.push({choices:[{delta:{},finish_reason:'tool_calls'}]});
++ }else chunks.push({choices:[{delta:{content:'Fixture response after the tool result.'},finish_reason:'stop'}]});
++ chunks.push({choices:[],usage:{prompt_tokens:200,completion_tokens:50}});
++ res.writeHead(200,{'Content-Type':'text/event-stream'});for(const chunk of chunks)res.write('data: '+JSON.stringify(chunk)+'\n\n');res.end('data: [DONE]\n\n');
++}).listen(port,'0.0.0.0',()=>console.log(`Disposable mock gateway listening on ${port}`));

+ # Funk Bot
+ 
+-Funk Bot is a local-first personal assistant workspace. This repository is a **partial implementation**, not the full persistent-agent platform: it provides password-protected, persistent Bot identities and conversations, configurable OpenAI-compatible gateways, model-profile fallback, and reported token usage. It provides two limited audited tools, but not a computer, autonomous routines, semantic memory, delegation, or groups. Do not use it for unattended work or assume it has the safety controls of a complete agent runtime.
++Funk Bot is a local-first personal assistant workspace. This repository is a **partial implementation**, not the full persistent-agent platform: it provides password-protected, persistent Bot identities and conversations, configurable OpenAI-compatible gateways, model-profile fallback, and reported token usage. It provides two limited audited tools, single-Bot missions and chief-led group missions, but not a computer, autonomous routines, or semantic memory. Do not use it for unattended work or assume it has the safety controls of a complete agent runtime.

This creates a mission, approves a note, and changes project data; do not run it against a real installation.

+ ## Current behavior and limitations
+ 
+ **Budget safeguards are not a guarantee of provider billing.** Funk Bot reserves against account and per-Bot daily/monthly caps before chat requests, but it depends on accurate configured prices, a conservative input-token bound, and the gateway honoring output limits and reporting usage. Tokenization overhead, gateway-added charges, incorrect prices, providers that ignore limits, and spending outside Funk Bot can exceed these estimates. Always set provider-side limits and do not leave runs unattended.
+ 
+ Open **Settings → Budget** to set caps and profile prices. The account and each Bot default to $5/day; monthly limits are disabled until configured. Periods use UTC. Each model round, including a follow-up after a tool call, reserves for every possible fallback; no configured price means the run is refused. Costs for new runs are calculated from reported input/output tokens and the profile's configured prices, not inferred from a model name. If an attempt fails, is interrupted, exceeds configured token bounds, or does not report usage, further spending is blocked until you verify its total in your gateway billing and enter the charge and source in Budget. These owner-supplied corrections are audited. Old usage without a cost must likewise be reconciled when it falls within a capped period. Existing Bots, keys, sprites and messages are not deleted by the budget migrations.
+ 
++- Projects contain an optional owner, project notes and links to existing missions. Mission totals come from linked runs and may be awaiting verification. The read-only workspace view shows flat `.txt` files belonging to the owner or linked mission assignees; these files remain Bot-local and can appear in multiple projects. Previews are limited to 64 KB and require secure descriptor-based file access (use Docker where unsupported). Unlinking a mission does not delete it or its files.
++- The Missions list shows the 100 most recent missions. A group contains two to six Bots including a Chief of Staff; the chief produces a structured plan, each member works sequentially, and the chief synthesizes the actual replies. Invalid plans fail rather than inventing delegation. Each run uses the same approvals and budgets as chat. Group membership is copied into a mission at creation. A queued mission starts when its Bot becomes free. Its result, cost and run events come from the actual run, and tool approvals use the same safety controls as chat. A restart marks unfinished missions failed rather than silently replaying them; check for completed tool side effects before retrying. Quick Mission creates a real mission.
+ - Each Bot has its own stored timeline and identity. The last 40 messages are sent as context; this is conversation history, not semantic memory. Deleting a Bot deletes its messages.
+ - The database uses SQLAlchemy connections with Alembic migrations, adopting existing slice databases without replacing their rows. SQL queries and migrations remain SQLite-specific; PostgreSQL support is not implemented. Back up the full data volume before upgrading.
+ - Chat runs in the backend and can finish after the browser closes, provided the backend keeps running. Run records and streamed events are stored in SQLite. Reopening a Bot reconnects to an active run; after a backend restart, unfinished runs are marked failed and surfaced in that Bot’s chat rather than automatically resumed. Run the backend with one worker only. Provider text streams through a sliding-window redactor for saved gateway keys and common key patterns. The filter deliberately delays a small tail of text and cannot detect all possible secrets.
+ - Profiles attempt entries in order for rate limits, server failures, connection errors, and empty responses. Client errors and partially emitted responses stop the chain. The gateway and selected model must support OpenAI-compatible streamed tool calls. If a prior attempt may have incurred an unknown charge, no tools are executed and the charge must be reconciled before more spending.
+ - Bots can request `web_fetch` and `write_note`; there is no shell tool. Web access is default-deny; configure exact hosts or domain suffixes in **Settings → Web access**. Deny rules override allow rules, every resolved address must be public, connections use the validated address, redirects/compression are refused, and requests are limited to 256 KiB and 10 seconds. Web pages remain untrusted and can contain misleading or malicious instructions; these safeguards are not a complete defense against prompt injection.
+-- `write_note` creates a new `.txt` file only within the individual Bot's workspace. The owner sees the redacted arguments that will actually execute and must choose **Approve once**, **Approve for this response** (same tool only, current run only), or **Deny**. Review the entire content before approving. Tool activity appears in chat and **Settings → Tool audit**. A pending approval can be stopped; an interrupted or restarted run is never replayed automatically. A completed tool action is not undone if a subsequent model round exceeds a cap or fails. Deleting a Bot deletes its tool audit and conversation, but leaves its workspace note files on disk and returns its sprite to the Vault. Redaction is heuristic, not a guarantee that secrets are removed.
++- `write_note` creates a new `.txt` file only within the individual Bot's workspace. The owner sees the redacted arguments that will actually execute and must choose **Approve once**, **Approve for this response** (same tool only, current run only), or **Deny**. Review the entire content before approving. Tool activity appears in chat and **Settings → Tool audit**. A pending approval can be stopped; an interrupted or restarted run is never replayed automatically. A completed tool action is not undone if a subsequent model round exceeds a cap or fails. Redaction is heuristic, not a guarantee that secrets are removed.
+ - Token totals come from reported usage. Known costs include configured-price token charges and owner-reconciled amounts; unknown charges are disclosed rather than treated as free. Caps are reservation-based estimates, not provider-enforced billing limits.
+ - Vault encryption protects database contents from casual inspection, but its key is stored alongside the data on the same host. Protect filesystem access and backups. Messages and provider output are redacted for saved gateway keys and common key patterns; no redaction is perfect.
+ - The authenticated `/api/events?since=0` endpoint exposes cursor-ordered run starts, message summaries, state changes, errors, and finishes recorded after this upgrade. Existing slice-2 events remain in per-run history and are not backfilled. Deleting a Bot deletes its event history. This is not a complete audit log. Beyond the two tools described above, no general search or file access, MCP, scheduler, webhook, sandbox, notifications, PWA, export, or browser/computer features are provided. The UI intentionally does not advertise those as working.

++def project_workspace_bots(c, project_id):
++    project=c.execute('SELECT owner_bot_id FROM projects WHERE id=?',(project_id,)).fetchone()
++    if not project: raise HTTPException(404, 'Project not found.')
++    ids={project['owner_bot_id']} if project['owner_bot_id'] else set()

++def open_workspace(bot_id):
++    # Never follow links or accept a caller-supplied directory outside DATA.
++    try:
++        if str(uuid.UUID(bot_id)) != bot_id: raise ValueError()
++    except ValueError: raise HTTPException(400, 'Invalid Bot workspace.')
++    if not hasattr(os,'O_NOFOLLOW') or not hasattr(os,'O_DIRECTORY') or os.open not in os.supports_dir_fd:
++        raise HTTPException(503, 'Secure workspace reads are not supported on this platform; use Docker.')
++    flags=os.O_RDONLY|os.O_DIRECTORY|os.O_NOFOLLOW
++    fds=[]
++    try:
++        fds.append(os.open(DATA,flags))
++        fds.append(os.open('workspaces',flags,dir_fd=fds[-1]))
++        return os.open(bot_id,flags,dir_fd=fds[-1])
++    except FileNotFoundError:
++        return None
++    except OSError as exc:
++        raise HTTPException(400, 'Could not safely access the workspace.') from exc
++    finally:
++        for fd in fds: os.close(fd)
++
++
++@app.get('/api/projects/{project_id}/files')
++def project_files(project_id: str, request: Request):
++    require_auth(request)
++    with db() as c: bot_ids=project_workspace_bots(c,project_id)
++    files=[]
++    for bot_id in sorted(bot_ids):
++        fd=open_workspace(bot_id)
++        if fd is None: continue
++        try:
++            with os.scandir(fd) as entries:
++                for entry in entries:
++                    if not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,79}\.txt',entry.name): continue
++                    try:
++                        info=entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
++                        if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode): files.append({'bot_id':bot_id,'name':entry.name,'size':info.st_size,'modified_at':info.st_mtime})
++                    except FileNotFoundError: continue
++        finally: os.close(fd)
++    return sorted(files,key=lambda item:(item['bot_id'],item['name']))

++            with os.fdopen(fd,'rb',closefd=False) as stream: data=stream.read(65537)

++            except UnicodeDecodeError: raise HTTPException(400, 'File is not UTF-8 text.')
++            return {'content':redact_text(text,configured_secrets()),'size':len(data),'modified_at':info.st_mtime}

++    finally: os.close(directory)

++### Docker smoke check (PowerShell)
++
++With Docker Desktop running, from the repository root run:
++
++```powershell
++.\scripts\docker-smoke.ps1
++```
++
++This builds and starts a separate temporary Compose project, checks `/api/health` through the frontend and verifies the database migration head. It exits nonzero on failure, stops its containers, and deliberately retains its isolated smoke volume. It does not use or remove existing installation volumes and does not test a real model gateway.

+ ## Character Vault
+ 
+ Open **Settings → Character Vault**, then import a ZIP of PNGs from Sprite Grid Slicer. The importer reads `CharacterName`, `CharacterRole`, `Tags` and `Notes` (and `funk:` equivalents); `CharacterName` or `funk:name` is required. ZIPs are limited to 20 MB, 500 files and 64 MB uncompressed; individual PNGs are limited to 8 MB and 16 megapixels. Invalid files and duplicate names or files are skipped with counts. Names and artwork are not sent to the interface until a character is assigned to a Bot. A new Bot gets a weighted random character without replacement until the draw pool is exhausted; existing Bots and an empty Vault use the built-in shapes. Deleting a Bot returns its character to the available pool if no other Bot has it.

++### Analytics, Lab and memory
++
++Analytics groups real runs and model rounds by their UTC start date, and approval decisions by decision date. Latency includes time waiting for approvals; the error rate counts failed runs among terminal runs (including cancellations). Costs are ledger estimates based on configured prices, not provider invoices. Pending or uncertain charges are counted separately and excluded from spend. Older usage without a linked reservation is shown under an unknown profile. CSV contains the same rows.
++
++Lab compares up to three configured profiles sequentially. Each call reserves budget and is counted in the ledger. It sends the tested prompt without Bot conversation history, memory or tools, and rejects unexpected tool calls. Lab runs do not add chat messages or write workspace files. A completed test can explicitly replace the Bot personality or save its results as a project note. A restart marks unfinished tests failed. It cannot prevent a model provider from storing a request; check that provider's policies.
++
++Per-Bot memory is managed in Lab. Entries can be edited, deleted and pinned, with a maximum of 50 entries, 4,000 characters per entry and 32,000 characters per Bot. Normal runs include up to 8,000 characters, pinned then most recent; the memory is described to the model as untrusted data. Known gateway keys and common secret patterns are redacted before storage, but redaction is not guaranteed: never put sensitive information in memory. Deleting a Bot deletes its memory.
++
+ ## Current behavior and limitations
+ 
+ **Budget safeguards are not a guarantee of provider billing.** Funk Bot reserves against account and per-Bot daily/monthly caps before chat requests, but it depends on accurate configured prices, a conservative input-token bound, and the gateway honoring output limits and reporting usage. Tokenization overhead, gateway-added charges, incorrect prices, providers that ignore limits, and spending outside Funk Bot can exceed these estimates. Always set provider-side limits and do not leave runs unattended.

+ Open **Settings → Character Vault**, then import a ZIP of PNGs from Sprite Grid Slicer. The importer reads `CharacterName`, `CharacterRole`, `Tags` and `Notes` (and `funk:` equivalents); `CharacterName` or `funk:name` is required. ZIPs are limited to 20 MB, 500 files and 64 MB uncompressed; individual PNGs are limited to 8 MB and 16 megapixels. Invalid files and duplicate names or files are skipped with counts. Names and artwork are not sent to the interface until a character is assigned to a Bot. A new Bot gets a weighted random character without replacement until the draw pool is exhausted; existing Bots and an empty Vault use the built-in shapes. Deleting a Bot returns its character to the available pool if no other Bot has it.
+ 
+-Character images are stored in the same private data volume as the database; back up the whole volume. Image routes require login and a Bot assignment. Files on your own machine cannot be hidden from an administrator with filesystem access. There is no CLI, reroll, collection browser, per-character animation map or bulk editing in this slice. Imported notes are shown on reveal but are not automatically injected into prompts.

The canvas is a visualization only: it makes no model calls. **Try demo** plays an explicitly labeled scripted meeting and shows pathfinding to and from the meeting room. ++**Gallery** is the home view. It shows assigned characters only; unassigned Vault art stays hidden. Search Bots, switch grid/list/cluster layout, or use the tag-based collection groups in the sidebar. At import, an optional collection tag is added to each newly imported character; duplicates are not modified. An untagged Bot appears in Uncategorized. The gallery paginates 60 Bots at a time and virtualizes visible rows; the sidebar limits its displayed Bot lists to 50, so use search to narrow them. Bot metadata is still fetched in one request, not server-paginated.
++
++Select a Bot to open its spotlight and chat. Quick Mission sends to the selected Bot through the same chat path. The Activity panel and status indicators come from recorded events. Runs today means `run.started` events since local midnight, not a count of historic runs that predate the event log. Last activity is the latest surviving event. No uptime or mission count is calculated. Upload or remove a private banner under **Settings → Appearance**; otherwise a gradient is shown.
++

++export type TeamBot={id:string;name:string;title:string;color:string;shape:string;character?:{name:string;role:string;tags:string[];avatar_url:string}|null};
++export type TeamEvent={id:number;bot_id:string|null;type:string;payload:Record<string,unknown>;created_at:number};
++export type Overview={bots:number;runs_today:number;last_activity:number|null;events:TeamEvent[];states:Record<string,string>};
++export const PAGE_SIZE=60;
++export function collections(bots:TeamBot[]){
++  const groups=new Map<string,TeamBot[]>();
++  for(const bot of bots){const tags=bot.character?.tags.length?bot.character.tags:['Uncategorized'];const seen=new Set<string>();for(const tag of tags){const key=tag.trim();if(!key||seen.has(key.toLowerCase()))continue;seen.add(key.toLowerCase());const existing=[...groups.keys()].find(k=>k.toLowerCase()===key.toLowerCase())||key;groups.set(existing,[...(groups.get(existing)||[]),bot])}}
++  return [...groups.entries()].sort(([a],[b])=>a.localeCompare(b));
++}
++export function describeEvent(e:TeamEvent,names:Map<string,string>){
++ const name=e.bot_id?(names.get(e.bot_id)||'Bot'):'Team';
++ switch(e.type){case 'message.sent':return `${name}: ${String(e.payload.summary||'')}`;case 'run.started':return `${name} started a run.`;case 'run.finished':return `${name} finished: ${String(e.payload.status||'unknown')}.`;case 'bot.state_changed':return `${name}: ${String(e.payload.state||'unknown')}.`;case 'error.raised':return `${name}: ${String(e.payload.message||'A run failed.')}`;default:return `${name}: ${e.type}`}
++}
++export function timeLabel(value:number|null){return value?new Date(value*1000).toLocaleString():'No recorded activity'}
++export function useOverview(enabled:boolean,botId=''){
++ const [data,setData]=useState<Overview|null>(null),[error,setError]=useState('');
++ useEffect(()=>{if(!enabled)return;const abort=new AbortController();let timer:ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
++  async function poll(){try{const date=new Date();date.setHours(0,0,0,0);const q=new URLSearchParams({day_start:String(date.getTime()/1000)});if(botId)q.set('bot_id',botId);const r=await fetch('/api/team/overview?'+q,{signal:abort.signal});if(!r.ok)throw Error('Could not load recorded activity.');const result=await r.json();if(!abort.signal.aborted){setData(result);setError('')}}catch(e){if(!abort.signal.aborted)setError((e as Error).message)}if(!abort.signal.aborted)timer=setTimeout(poll,3000)}
++  void poll();return()=>{abort.abort();clearTimeout(timer)};
++ },[enabled,botId]);return {data,error};
++}
++export function Activity({events,bots}:{events:TeamEvent[];bots:TeamBot[]}){const names=useMemo(()=>new Map(bots.map(b=>[b.id,b.name])),[bots]);return <div className="team-activity">{events.length?events.map(e=><div className="team-event" key={e.id}><span className="event-spark">✧</span><div>{describeEvent(e,names)}<small>{timeLabel(e.created_at)}</small></div></div>):<p className="team-empty">No recorded activity yet.</p>}</div>}

+ Open **Settings → Character Vault**, then import a ZIP of PNGs from Sprite Grid Slicer. The importer reads `CharacterName`, `CharacterRole`, `Tags` and `Notes` (and `funk:` equivalents); `CharacterName` or `funk:name` is required. ZIPs are limited to 20 MB, 500 files and 64 MB uncompressed; individual PNGs are limited to 8 MB and 16 megapixels. Invalid files and duplicate names or files are skipped with counts. Names and artwork are not sent to the interface until a character is assigned to a Bot. A new Bot gets a weighted random character without replacement until the draw pool is exhausted; existing Bots and an empty Vault use the built-in shapes. Deleting a Bot returns its character to the available pool if no other Bot has it.
+ 
++New Bots pick a job preset or custom job, with editable instructions; their name comes from the drawn Vault character, or from the fallback name if the Vault is empty. Existing names and job titles stay unchanged. For an existing Bot without a sprite, open its spotlight and choose **Give me a sprite**; explicitly choose whether to keep the name or adopt the character name. The job title is included in the system prompt. The Vault role is an archetype shown in the spotlight, not a job title.
++
+ Character images are stored in the same private data volume as the database; back up the whole volume. Image routes require login and a Bot assignment. Files on your own machine cannot be hidden from an administrator with filesystem access. There is no CLI, reroll, per-character animation map or bulk editing in this slice. Imported notes are shown on reveal but are not automatically injected into prompts.

+ ## Current behavior and limitations
+ 
++**No spending caps are implemented yet.** Funk Bot cannot prevent a runaway run from consuming gateway credits. Set limits with your provider and do not leave the app unattended.
++
+ - Each Bot has its own stored timeline and identity. The last 40 messages are sent as context; this is conversation history, not semantic memory. Deleting a Bot deletes its messages.
+ - The database uses SQLAlchemy connections with Alembic migrations, adopting existing slice databases without replacing their rows. SQL queries and migrations remain SQLite-specific; PostgreSQL support is not implemented. Back up the full data volume before upgrading.
+ - Chat runs in the backend and can finish after the browser closes, provided the backend keeps running. Run records and streamed events are stored in SQLite. Reopening a Bot reconnects to an active run; after a backend restart, unfinished runs are marked failed and surfaced in that Bot’s chat rather than automatically resumed. Run the backend with one worker only. Provider text streams through a sliding-window redactor for saved gateway keys and common key patterns. The filter deliberately delays a small tail of text and cannot detect all possible secrets.

++### Visual-pass browser check
++
++The `visual-*` screenshots show Gallery, Roster, and Office at desktop and phone widths, plus the phone sidebar. They use a **fresh disposable installation**, 12 Bots assigned synthetic Vault sprites from the two-image identity fixture, and one fallback Bot. The visual check makes no model calls, but it creates Bots and imports artwork: **never run it against your real installation**. Start a separate fresh test installation and use its one-time setup code:
++
++```powershell
++Set-Location frontend
++npm ci
++npx playwright install chromium
++$env:E2E_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
++$env:E2E_SETUP_TOKEN = "your-disposable-setup-code"
++npm run test:visual
++```
++
+ ## Current behavior and limitations
+ 
+ **No spending caps are implemented yet.** Funk Bot cannot prevent a runaway run from consuming gateway credits. Set limits with your provider and do not leave the app unattended.

+# Runs only an isolated disposable Compose project. Never removes volumes.
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+$project = "funkbot-smoke-$([guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0,12))"
+$composeFile = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'smoke-compose.yml'
+$started = $false
+$failed = $false
+try {
+    docker compose version
+    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Docker Compose is not available.' }
+    $started = $true
+    docker compose -p $project -f $composeFile up --build -d
+    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The isolated smoke stack failed to build or start.' }
+    $binding = docker compose -p $project -f $composeFile port frontend 3000
+    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or "$binding" -notmatch ':(\d+)\s*$') { throw 'Could not determine the frontend smoke port.' }
+    $port = [regex]::Match("$binding", ":(\d+)\s*$").Groups[1].Value
+    $healthy = $false
+    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 90; $i++) {
+        try {
+            $health = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:$port/api/health" -TimeoutSec 3
+            if ($health.status -eq 'ok') { $healthy = $true; break }
+        } catch { Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }
+    }
+    if (-not $healthy) { throw 'The frontend proxy did not return a healthy API response.' }
+    $check = "import sqlite3; from alembic.script import ScriptDirectory; from alembic.config import Config; c=Config(); c.set_main_option('script_location','funkbot/migrations'); head=ScriptDirectory.from_config(c).get_current_head(); db=sqlite3.connect('/data/funk.db'); actual=db.execute('select version_num from alembic_version').fetchone()[0]; assert actual == head, f'migration {actual} != {head}'; print('Migration head:',actual)"
+    docker compose -p $project -f $composeFile exec -T backend python -c $check
+    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The database is not at the current migration head.' }
+    Write-Host "Smoke test passed at http://127.0.0.1:$port/api/health (project $project)."
+} catch {
+    Write-Error -ErrorRecord $_ -ErrorAction Continue
+    $failed = $true
+} finally {
+    if ($started) {
+        docker compose -p $project -f $composeFile down
+        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Error 'Could not stop the isolated smoke stack.' -ErrorAction Continue; $failed = $true }
+        Write-Host "The isolated $project data volume was retained; existing installation volumes were not touched."
+    }
+}
+if ($failed) { exit 1 }
+exit 0
